title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'yoga' from the previous page. Contravariant invariants of a simplicial set X_* with values in a complete category B, which turn colimits in X_* into limits, correspond to simplicial objects of B. For B = (Ens) the invariant attached to a simplicial set K_* is simply the representable functor X_* ↦ K_*(X_*) = Hom(X_*, K_*). For B = (Ab), K_* is a simplicial abelian group, and the represented functor automatically takes values in abelian groups. The same holds for any algebraic structure 'expressible purely in terms of limits' (groups, rings, modules over rings): an internal such structure on K_* makes Hom(-, K_*) take values in that structure. In modern terms these are finite-limit, Lawvere-type or essentially algebraic theories.

Grothendieck then states the methodological programme. Invariants given directly by (co)simplicial objects of A or B are too 'gros' and 'frustes': they are not homotopy invariants. One should put on these big invariants a minimum of reasonable extra structure, for example chain or cochain complexes, or cosimplicial (commutative) algebras. In the corresponding category one inverts the arrows coming from weak homotopy equivalences in Ss, i.e. passes to a category of fractions, a localization or homotopy category. The resulting invariant is coarser in content but subtler in definition and less redundant. It captures the homotopy type more or less completely, or some aspect of it. This is the general philosophy behind models of homotopy types by cochain or cosimplicial algebras: rational homotopy theory, and, in the context of this 1976 lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex, presumably algebras with divided powers.

Finally he records the Dold–Kan correspondence, which he calls Dold–Puppe, for any additive Karoubian (idempotent-complete) category A. There are inverse equivalences ND: A_* → A_. (normalized or non-degenerate chain complex) and DP_*: A_. → A_* between simplicial objects and non-negatively graded chain complexes. He fixes the notational convention that K_* and K_. denote corresponding avatars. He correctly notes that 'every projector has a kernel' is equivalent to 'every projector has a cokernel' in an additive category. The next page carries out the dual cosimplicial/cochain version and the bookkeeping that forces the notation K_[n].
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.
On the previous page, 'commutent aux lim' for contravariant invariants should read 'transforment les lim inductives en lim projectives'; this is a slip of wording only.

The Dold–Kan equivalence is usually credited to Dold (1958) and Kan (1958); Dold–Puppe (1961) is the paper extending it to non-additive functors. Grothendieck's name for it is a naming convention, not an error.

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving contravariant invariants of simplicial sets with values in a complete category are represented by simplicial objects. Algebraic structures defined by limits transfer to the represented functors.
ideas.modern_name: Representable functors / internal algebraic structures (Lawvere theories, finite-limit sketches); nerve–realization adjunction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958, adjoint functors); Lawvere (1963) for algebraic theories
ideas.where_published: Internal group/ring objects via representable functors: FGA, SGA 3 exposé I; also Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Programme: equip the coarse (co)simplicial invariants with minimal algebraic structure (chain complexes, cosimplicial algebras) and localize at the images of weak equivalences, to obtain homotopy-type invariants.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic models for homotopy types via localization (homotopical algebra; rational homotopy à la Quillen/Sullivan; cochain-algebra models à la Mandell, Toën's affine stacks)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) and its discussion of 'schematization' of homotopy types / modelizers; the 1976 IHÉS lecture itself is not published

ideas.what: Dold–Kan equivalence between simplicial objects and non-negative chain complexes in any idempotent-complete additive category (and dually for cosimplicial objects and cochain complexes).
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence for Karoubian additive categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold (1958), Kan (1958); general additive idempotent-complete form folklore, e.g. Lurie, Higher Algebra 1.2.3

missed.claim: In a 1975–76 lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex, Grothendieck frames homotopy theory as localizing categories of structured (co)simplicial invariants, such as cosimplicial algebras and cochain complexes, at weak equivalences. He aims to capture the homotopy type 'more or less completely'. This anticipates the later programme of modelling (p-adic or integral) homotopy types by structured cochain algebras (Mandell, Toën's affine stacks, Pursuing Stacks' schematization). It does so in an explicitly divided-power / crystalline context, but here only as a programme statement.
missed.quote: d'inverser les flèches qui sont obtenues à partir d'équivalences d'homotopie dans Ss, et de passer à des "catégories de fractions" ... exprimera donc de façon plus ou moins complète le type d'homotopie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents an early (pre-Pursuing Stacks) date for Grothendieck's idea of algebraic models of homotopy types via cosimplicial/divided-power algebras. That is of historical interest for the genealogy of Mandell's theorem and of affine stacks. No new mathematics appears on this page itself.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly expository: representability, a standard localization philosophy, and the Dold–Kan correspondence. The only point of interest is the early dating and the divided-power context of the 'models of homotopy types by structured cosimplicial algebras' programme.
transcription_corrections: 'le théorème [?] de Dold-Puppe' is more likely 'la théorie de Dold-Puppe'.
'à compter [?] de foncteurs représentables' is likely 'à partir de foncteurs représentables'.
'invariants "gros" cependant [?]' is likely 'invariants "gros" en question'; 'munis du dicton [?]' is unclear, possibly 'suivant les cas'.
'(plus "grossier"' should be read as a parenthetical insertion: 'L'invariant ainsi obtenu (plus "grossier" bien sûr, mais plus subtil dans sa définition, et moins "redondant")'.
